sources.excerpt: Alviso datacenter construction update Alviso datacenter construction begins in California Microsoft is expanding its datacenter infrastructure with construction at our new Alviso site in California. Construction hours Work will take place Monday through Friday, from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Should additional hours be required, HITT will adhere to the local requirements. Staying connected We’re committed to keeping the community informed. Visit our Microsoft in your community page for updates.

sources.name: Microsoft Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project
sources.excerpt: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project On Thursday, June 18, Microsoft marked an important milestone in La Porte, Indiana, with a groundbreaking event for its new datacenter project, alongside local leaders and community partners. In addition to the datacenter groundbreaking, Microsoft celebrated the signing of a partnership with Ivy Tech Community College to launch its first Microsoft Datacenter Academy in Indiana. The event brought together elected officials, community stakeholders, and partners to highlight progress on site development and reinforce Microsoft’s commitment to investing in the region through jobs, infrastructure, and long-term community engagement. Brad Smith, Microsoft Vice Chair and President, delivered remarks as part of Microsoft’s Community-First Infrastructure initiative, joining the La Porte mayor and local leaders. “AI infrastructure is driving demand for skilled trades nationwide,” said Smith. “We’re committed to helping fill these jobs with people in the communities where we operate. Our Datacenter Academy agreement with Ivy Tech Community College will do just that by equipping people in Indiana with the skills to pursue the jobs we will create here.” Beyond the thousands of construction jobs, the first phase of the new datacenter is expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs. It will grow local tax revenues to support schools and the broader community for generations. The campus will be designed with the latest energy efficient and closed-loop liquid cooling technologies to conserve natural resources. And Microsoft will enhance the surrounding ecosystem to strengthen flood protection and natural habitat.

sources.name: Microsoft Responsible development in Prince William County
sources.excerpt: Responsible development in Prince William County An update on our environmental work at the proposed Wellington datacenter site In 2024, Microsoft purchased land in Prince William County, Virginia for the purpose of datacenter development. While datacenter development has yet to commence, we have started the process of applying for permits. The project remains in the early planning and permitting stage with actual datacenter construction still a long way off. Microsoft is committed to responsible development on this site, respecting the unique and challenging environmental history of this land. We’re working with local partners to carry out all necessary environmental remediation and ensure our future plans have appropriately considered the local context and adequately protect the community from future environmental degradation. This environmental work is the reason that we’ve started the planning and permitting process so early – taking the necessary time to ensure plans are advanced responsibly, in compliance with all federal, state and local regulations. The approximately 124-acre property is located on Wellington Road in Gainesville, Virginia, and has a history of industrial use that predates Microsoft’s ownership and resulted in soil and groundwater contamination. Cleanup of this pre-existing contamination continues under a longstanding U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) consent order, which outlines the cleanup requirements and mandates ongoing reporting to the EPA. Under government oversight, the prior industrial operator remains responsible for maintaining the site’s groundwater treatment and monitoring systems and addressing the contamination. Microsoft is funding and providing technical support to relocate and modernize the treatment infrastructure so cleanup can continue as property plans advance. Microsoft and the previous industrial operator are coordinating with the EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Prince William County, and other agencies to ensure that our plans comply with all existing regulations and any necessary environmental reviews and approvals are completed before any work moves forward. Additional information about the property’s cleanup history can be found here: EPA RCRA ID: VAD023741705 | US EPA As plans are developed, Microsoft’s approach will be to avoid and minimize impacts on wetlands, waterways, and other natural resources. If impacts cannot be avoided, appropriate permits would be sought, and mitigation measures such as funding for stream and wetland restoration would be incorporated into the project. As construction moves forward, environmental controls will address stormwater, erosion, soil, dust, and waste. Additionally, materials will be evaluated and managed in accordance with applicable requirements. We will continue to share updates with the local community as plans advance and key milestones are reached.

Jobs The project is expected to generate more than 9,000 construction jobs, as well as 1,000 ongoing project-supported jobs within the first two years after construction is complete. Local suppliers, vendors, contractors and residents will be prioritized. Oracle is currently hiring for a range of permanent positions in tech, engineering and operations, as well as offering a paid work trainee program to help launch a career in tech without experience. Community Impact This AI data center will yield an estimated $30 million annually in local economic benefits for the City of Abilene and Taylor County, supporting schools, emergency services, roads, and county programs. Energy The Abilene AI data center connects directly to the ERCOT grid, allowing us to draw from the region's robust and growing supply of renewable energy, including wind, which often goes underutilized in the area. To support grid stability, the Abilene campus uses GE Vernova’s modern natural gas turbines for backup power. The turbines are equipped with Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which transforms nitrogen oxides (NOx) into harmless water vapor and nitrogen through a catalytic converter, producing 90% lower emissions than conventional gas- or diesel-powered reciprocating engines, with little to no methane slip. Water The Abilene AI data center uses a one-time fill, closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system that significantly reduces water consumption. Each building will use roughly 50,000 gallons per year for cooling maintenance, which is under the yearly water use of a single American household—an exceptionally small amount for a facility of this size. sources.excerpt: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project On Thursday, June 18, Microsoft marked an important milestone in La Porte, Indiana, with a groundbreaking event for its new datacenter project, alongside local leaders and community partners. In addition to the datacenter groundbreaking, Microsoft celebrated the signing of a partnership with Ivy Tech Community College to launch its first Microsoft Datacenter Academy in Indiana. The event brought together elected officials, community stakeholders, and partners to highlight progress on site development and reinforce Microsoft’s commitment to investing in the region through jobs, infrastructure, and long-term community engagement. Brad Smith, Microsoft Vice Chair and President, delivered remarks as part of Microsoft’s Community-First Infrastructure initiative, joining the La Porte mayor and local leaders. “AI infrastructure is driving demand for skilled trades nationwide,” said Smith. “We’re committed to helping fill these jobs with people in the communities where we operate. Our Datacenter Academy agreement with Ivy Tech Community College will do just that by equipping people in Indiana with the skills to pursue the jobs we will create here.” Beyond the thousands of construction jobs, the first phase of the new datacenter is expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs. It will grow local tax revenues to support schools and the broader community for generations. The campus will be designed with the latest energy efficient and closed-loop liquid cooling technologies to conserve natural resources. And Microsoft will enhance the surrounding ecosystem to strengthen flood protection and natural habitat.

September 2026: Construction update Work continues to move forward on the first building at the Lyle Creek datacenter site, with key milestones achieved on the building structure and exterior. The building exterior is in its final stages of completion. Framing and drywall work has started and continues to progress throughout the building. Work on underground infrastructure also continues to support the site and upcoming equipment deliveries. Mechanical and electrical work has begun, and additional interior work continues. Work is also beginning on additional building areas to support upcoming phases of construction. We appreciate the community’s patience as construction progresses and will continue to provide updates on significant milestones. May 2026: Construction update Work is advancing across multiple areas of the site, with key milestones reached in foundations and early structural development. Construction activity is moving forward as crews complete early phases and begin vertical construction: Underground work, foundations, and slab installation are complete for several buildings. February 2026: Construction update At the Lyle Creek site, Microsoft’s general contractor, Whiting‑Turner, will begin initial site preparation once weather conditions allow. sources.name: Microsoft Responsible development in Prince William County
sources.excerpt: Responsible development in Prince William County An update on our environmental work at the proposed Wellington datacenter site In 2024, Microsoft purchased land in Prince William County, Virginia for the purpose of datacenter development. While datacenter development has yet to commence, we have started the process of applying for permits. The project remains in the early planning and permitting stage with actual datacenter construction still a long way off. Microsoft is committed to responsible development on this site, respecting the unique and challenging environmental history of this land. We’re working with local partners to carry out all necessary environmental remediation and ensure our future plans have appropriately considered the local context and adequately protect the community from future environmental degradation. This environmental work is the reason that we’ve started the planning and permitting process so early – taking the necessary time to ensure plans are advanced responsibly, in compliance with all federal, state and local regulations. The approximately 124-acre property is located on Wellington Road in Gainesville, Virginia, and has a history of industrial use that predates Microsoft’s ownership and resulted in soil and groundwater contamination. Cleanup of this pre-existing contamination continues under a longstanding U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) consent order, which outlines the cleanup requirements and mandates ongoing reporting to the EPA. Under government oversight, the prior industrial operator remains responsible for maintaining the site’s groundwater treatment and monitoring systems and addressing the contamination. Microsoft is funding and providing technical support to relocate and modernize the treatment infrastructure so cleanup can continue as property plans advance. Microsoft and the previous industrial operator are coordinating with the EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Prince William County, and other agencies to ensure that our plans comply with all existing regulations and any necessary environmental reviews and approvals are completed before any work moves forward. Additional information about the property’s cleanup history can be found here: EPA RCRA ID: VAD023741705 | US EPA As plans are developed, Microsoft’s approach will be to avoid and minimize impacts on wetlands, waterways, and other natural resources. If impacts cannot be avoided, appropriate permits would be sought, and mitigation measures such as funding for stream and wetland restoration would be incorporated into the project. As construction moves forward, environmental controls will address stormwater, erosion, soil, dust, and waste. Additionally, materials will be evaluated and managed in accordance with applicable requirements. We will continue to share updates with the local community as plans advance and key milestones are reached.

Community Impact This AI data center will yield an estimated $30 million annually in local economic benefits for the City of Abilene and Taylor County, supporting schools, emergency services, roads, and county programs. Energy The Abilene AI data center connects directly to the ERCOT grid, allowing us to draw from the region's robust and growing supply of renewable energy, including wind, which often goes underutilized in the area. To support grid stability, the Abilene campus uses GE Vernova’s modern natural gas turbines for backup power. The turbines are equipped with Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which transforms nitrogen oxides (NOx) into harmless water vapor and nitrogen through a catalytic converter, producing 90% lower emissions than conventional gas- or diesel-powered reciprocating engines, with little to no methane slip. Water The Abilene AI data center uses a one-time fill, closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system that significantly reduces water consumption. Each building will use roughly 50,000 gallons per year for cooling maintenance, which is under the yearly water use of a single American household—an exceptionally small amount for a facility of this size. sources.name: Microsoft Alviso datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Alviso datacenter construction update Alviso datacenter construction begins in California Microsoft is expanding its datacenter infrastructure with construction at our new Alviso site in California. This update marks the beginning of a multi-phase effort to prepare the land for future datacenter development, supporting the growing demand for cloud services and digital transformation. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction overview HITT Contracting Inc. is the general contractor for the Alviso datacenter. Construction began in fall 2025 with initial work focused on earthmoving and soil remediation. Site preparation work is expected to be completed by summer 2026. We’re working closely with HITT to keep neighbors informed ahead of any major construction activity. Construction hours Work will take place Monday through Friday, from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Should additional hours be required, HITT will adhere to the local requirements. Staying connected We’re committed to keeping the community informed. Visit our Microsoft in your community page for updates.

sources.name: Microsoft Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project
sources.excerpt: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project On Thursday, June 18, Microsoft marked an important milestone in La Porte, Indiana, with a groundbreaking event for its new datacenter project, alongside local leaders and community partners. In addition to the datacenter groundbreaking, Microsoft celebrated the signing of a partnership with Ivy Tech Community College to launch its first Microsoft Datacenter Academy in Indiana. The event brought together elected officials, community stakeholders, and partners to highlight progress on site development and reinforce Microsoft’s commitment to investing in the region through jobs, infrastructure, and long-term community engagement. Brad Smith, Microsoft Vice Chair and President, delivered remarks as part of Microsoft’s Community-First Infrastructure initiative, joining the La Porte mayor and local leaders. “AI infrastructure is driving demand for skilled trades nationwide,” said Smith. “We’re committed to helping fill these jobs with people in the communities where we operate. Our Datacenter Academy agreement with Ivy Tech Community College will do just that by equipping people in Indiana with the skills to pursue the jobs we will create here.” Beyond the thousands of construction jobs, the first phase of the new datacenter is expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs. It will grow local tax revenues to support schools and the broader community for generations. The campus will be designed with the latest energy efficient and closed-loop liquid cooling technologies to conserve natural resources. And Microsoft will enhance the surrounding ecosystem to strengthen flood protection and natural habitat.

sources.name: Microsoft Responsible development in Prince William County
sources.excerpt: Responsible development in Prince William County An update on our environmental work at the proposed Wellington datacenter site In 2024, Microsoft purchased land in Prince William County, Virginia for the purpose of datacenter development. While datacenter development has yet to commence, we have started the process of applying for permits. The project remains in the early planning and permitting stage with actual datacenter construction still a long way off. Microsoft is committed to responsible development on this site, respecting the unique and challenging environmental history of this land. We’re working with local partners to carry out all necessary environmental remediation and ensure our future plans have appropriately considered the local context and adequately protect the community from future environmental degradation. This environmental work is the reason that we’ve started the planning and permitting process so early – taking the necessary time to ensure plans are advanced responsibly, in compliance with all federal, state and local regulations. The approximately 124-acre property is located on Wellington Road in Gainesville, Virginia, and has a history of industrial use that predates Microsoft’s ownership and resulted in soil and groundwater contamination. Cleanup of this pre-existing contamination continues under a longstanding U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) consent order, which outlines the cleanup requirements and mandates ongoing reporting to the EPA. Under government oversight, the prior industrial operator remains responsible for maintaining the site’s groundwater treatment and monitoring systems and addressing the contamination. Microsoft is funding and providing technical support to relocate and modernize the treatment infrastructure so cleanup can continue as property plans advance. Microsoft and the previous industrial operator are coordinating with the EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Prince William County, and other agencies to ensure that our plans comply with all existing regulations and any necessary environmental reviews and approvals are completed before any work moves forward. Additional information about the property’s cleanup history can be found here: EPA RCRA ID: VAD023741705 | US EPA As plans are developed, Microsoft’s approach will be to avoid and minimize impacts on wetlands, waterways, and other natural resources. If impacts cannot be avoided, appropriate permits would be sought, and mitigation measures such as funding for stream and wetland restoration would be incorporated into the project. As construction moves forward, environmental controls will address stormwater, erosion, soil, dust, and waste. Additionally, materials will be evaluated and managed in accordance with applicable requirements. We will continue to share updates with the local community as plans advance and key milestones are reached.

Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction update July 2026 As part of ongoing preparation at our datacenter site in Mount Pleasant, crews will begin moving soil materials between areas of the project site. Construction overview Starting on or around July 13, 2026, construction teams will begin hauling soil from one area of the site to another to support future development. This work is expected to continue for approximately eight weeks, depending on weather, permitting, and construction schedules. During this time, neighbors may notice: Increased truck traffic in and around the site. Movement of soil and construction materials. Stockpiling and early site preparation activity. Traffic and site operations Construction vehicles will use designated haul routes and approved access points within the project area. Teams will actively coordinate operations to help manage traffic flow and reduce impacts to the surrounding community. A map of the planned haul route is included for reference. Construction hours Construction activity will take place during permitted local construction hours. If work outside of these hours is required, it will follow all applicable local regulations. Staying connected We are committed to keeping our neighbors informed about construction activities. Questions about construction? Please contact Walsh Construction at MPDC@walshgroup.com or call 312-497-6967. Questions about other aspects of the project? Contact WisconsinDC@microsoft.com or leave a message at 608-535-3569. Learn more at local.microsoft.com/Wisconsin . June 2026: Community Connect Open House Microsoft hosted a Community Connect open house on June 23, 2026, at the Fountain Banquet Hall. The event provided an opportunity for community members to learn more about the Mount Pleasant datacenter project, hear the latest updates, and connect directly with subject matter experts. Attendees were able to ask questions and engage with project team members about ongoing construction activities, community investments, and upcoming milestones. Thank you to everyone who joined us and shared their feedback. Boards for Mount Pleasant Community Connect Open House April 2026: Community Office Hours Microsoft hosted “community office hours” for neighbors of the Mount Pleasant datacenter on April 9, 2026, at the Mount Pleasant Village Hall Ebe Auditorium. The informal session provided an opportunity for community members to hear about Mount Pleasant datacenter project updates, ask questions, and learn more about local investments and job opportunities. Thank you to everyone who participated. For those who were unable to attend, a link is available to view the presentation materials shared during the session. Boards for Mount Pleasant community office hours Construction update March 2026 Construction overview Construction continues at the Mount Pleasant Datacenter Campus , with progress underway across multiple phases. Phase 1—KR & 90th Work in this phase is nearing completion. Crews are finalizing interior work in several buildings and completing landscaping. Construction for Phase 1 is anticipated to be complete by spring 2026 . Phase 2—KR & H Construction activities for Phase 2 are ongoing and focused on expanding the site. Current work includes foundation installation, steel erection, and underground utility installation. This phase is scheduled to be completed in early 2028 . Phase 3—Durand & Hewitt Memorial Drive Preliminary earthwork is underway to prepare the site for future construction. To support construction operations, there are currently four site entrances: Gate 1: Highway KR Gate 2: Braun Road Gate 3: County Road H Gate 4: County Road H Construction schedule and activity Work is expected to begin in mid March , depending on ground conditions as seasonal thaw continues. To help reduce dust and debris on nearby roads, street sweepers will operate for approximately 10 hours per day . Tire wash systems are also in place at site exits to help keep surrounding roadways clean. Construction hours Construction activities are conducted in compliance with the Village of Mount Pleasant code. Work may take place between 6 AM and 10 PM, seven days per week . We appreciate your continued patience and cooperation as our crews move into the next phase of construction. Walsh Construction remains committed to minimizing disruption and maintaining safe, clean roadways throughout the project. Questions about construction? sources.excerpt: Abilene, Texas Data Center Abilene Data Center Facts Open all Construction Timeline and Delivery AI workloads went live less than a year after construction began. Jobs The project is expected to generate more than 9,000 construction jobs, as well as 1,000 ongoing project-supported jobs within the first two years after construction is complete. Local suppliers, vendors, contractors and residents will be prioritized. Oracle is currently hiring for a range of permanent positions in tech, engineering and operations, as well as offering a paid work trainee program to help launch a career in tech without experience. Community Impact This AI data center will yield an estimated $30 million annually in local economic benefits for the City of Abilene and Taylor County, supporting schools, emergency services, roads, and county programs. Energy The Abilene AI data center connects directly to the ERCOT grid, allowing us to draw from the region's robust and growing supply of renewable energy, including wind, which often goes underutilized in the area. To support grid stability, the Abilene campus uses GE Vernova’s modern natural gas turbines for backup power. The turbines are equipped with Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which transforms nitrogen oxides (NOx) into harmless water vapor and nitrogen through a catalytic converter, producing 90% lower emissions than conventional gas- or diesel-powered reciprocating engines, with little to no methane slip. Water The Abilene AI data center uses a one-time fill, closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system that significantly reduces water consumption. Each building will use roughly 50,000 gallons per year for cooling maintenance, which is under the yearly water use of a single American household—an exceptionally small amount for a facility of this size. Size The campus consists of eight buildings on 1,100 acres, encompassing 4 million square feet of building space. Interested in a Career at an Oracle Data Center? Datacenters also support businesses, hospitals, schools, and governments. Datacenter buildings house thousands of computer servers and data storage devices connected to the internet. sources.name: Microsoft Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project
sources.excerpt: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project On Thursday, June 18, Microsoft marked an important milestone in La Porte, Indiana, with a groundbreaking event for its new datacenter project, alongside local leaders and community partners. In addition to the datacenter groundbreaking, Microsoft celebrated the signing of a partnership with Ivy Tech Community College to launch its first Microsoft Datacenter Academy in Indiana. The event brought together elected officials, community stakeholders, and partners to highlight progress on site development and reinforce Microsoft’s commitment to investing in the region through jobs, infrastructure, and long-term community engagement. Brad Smith, Microsoft Vice Chair and President, delivered remarks as part of Microsoft’s Community-First Infrastructure initiative, joining the La Porte mayor and local leaders. “AI infrastructure is driving demand for skilled trades nationwide,” said Smith. “We’re committed to helping fill these jobs with people in the communities where we operate. Our Datacenter Academy agreement with Ivy Tech Community College will do just that by equipping people in Indiana with the skills to pursue the jobs we will create here.” Beyond the thousands of construction jobs, the first phase of the new datacenter is expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs. It will grow local tax revenues to support schools and the broader community for generations. The campus will be designed with the latest energy efficient and closed-loop liquid cooling technologies to conserve natural resources. And Microsoft will enhance the surrounding ecosystem to strengthen flood protection and natural habitat.

sources.name: Microsoft Responsible development in Prince William County
sources.excerpt: Responsible development in Prince William County An update on our environmental work at the proposed Wellington datacenter site In 2024, Microsoft purchased land in Prince William County, Virginia for the purpose of datacenter development. While datacenter development has yet to commence, we have started the process of applying for permits. The project remains in the early planning and permitting stage with actual datacenter construction still a long way off. Microsoft is committed to responsible development on this site, respecting the unique and challenging environmental history of this land. We’re working with local partners to carry out all necessary environmental remediation and ensure our future plans have appropriately considered the local context and adequately protect the community from future environmental degradation. This environmental work is the reason that we’ve started the planning and permitting process so early – taking the necessary time to ensure plans are advanced responsibly, in compliance with all federal, state and local regulations. The approximately 124-acre property is located on Wellington Road in Gainesville, Virginia, and has a history of industrial use that predates Microsoft’s ownership and resulted in soil and groundwater contamination. Cleanup of this pre-existing contamination continues under a longstanding U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) consent order, which outlines the cleanup requirements and mandates ongoing reporting to the EPA. Under government oversight, the prior industrial operator remains responsible for maintaining the site’s groundwater treatment and monitoring systems and addressing the contamination. Microsoft is funding and providing technical support to relocate and modernize the treatment infrastructure so cleanup can continue as property plans advance. Microsoft and the previous industrial operator are coordinating with the EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Prince William County, and other agencies to ensure that our plans comply with all existing regulations and any necessary environmental reviews and approvals are completed before any work moves forward. Additional information about the property’s cleanup history can be found here: EPA RCRA ID: VAD023741705 | US EPA As plans are developed, Microsoft’s approach will be to avoid and minimize impacts on wetlands, waterways, and other natural resources. If impacts cannot be avoided, appropriate permits would be sought, and mitigation measures such as funding for stream and wetland restoration would be incorporated into the project. As construction moves forward, environmental controls will address stormwater, erosion, soil, dust, and waste. Additionally, materials will be evaluated and managed in accordance with applicable requirements. We will continue to share updates with the local community as plans advance and key milestones are reached.

Energy The Abilene AI data center connects directly to the ERCOT grid, allowing us to draw from the region's robust and growing supply of renewable energy, including wind, which often goes underutilized in the area. To support grid stability, the Abilene campus uses GE Vernova’s modern natural gas turbines for backup power. The turbines are equipped with Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which transforms nitrogen oxides (NOx) into harmless water vapor and nitrogen through a catalytic converter, producing 90% lower emissions than conventional gas- or diesel-powered reciprocating engines, with little to no methane slip. sources.name: Microsoft Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project
sources.excerpt: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project On Thursday, June 18, Microsoft marked an important milestone in La Porte, Indiana, with a groundbreaking event for its new datacenter project, alongside local leaders and community partners. In addition to the datacenter groundbreaking, Microsoft celebrated the signing of a partnership with Ivy Tech Community College to launch its first Microsoft Datacenter Academy in Indiana. The event brought together elected officials, community stakeholders, and partners to highlight progress on site development and reinforce Microsoft’s commitment to investing in the region through jobs, infrastructure, and long-term community engagement. Brad Smith, Microsoft Vice Chair and President, delivered remarks as part of Microsoft’s Community-First Infrastructure initiative, joining the La Porte mayor and local leaders. “AI infrastructure is driving demand for skilled trades nationwide,” said Smith. “We’re committed to helping fill these jobs with people in the communities where we operate. Our Datacenter Academy agreement with Ivy Tech Community College will do just that by equipping people in Indiana with the skills to pursue the jobs we will create here.” Beyond the thousands of construction jobs, the first phase of the new datacenter is expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs. It will grow local tax revenues to support schools and the broader community for generations. The campus will be designed with the latest energy efficient and closed-loop liquid cooling technologies to conserve natural resources. And Microsoft will enhance the surrounding ecosystem to strengthen flood protection and natural habitat.

sources.name: Microsoft Responsible development in Prince William County
sources.excerpt: Responsible development in Prince William County An update on our environmental work at the proposed Wellington datacenter site In 2024, Microsoft purchased land in Prince William County, Virginia for the purpose of datacenter development. While datacenter development has yet to commence, we have started the process of applying for permits. The project remains in the early planning and permitting stage with actual datacenter construction still a long way off. Microsoft is committed to responsible development on this site, respecting the unique and challenging environmental history of this land. We’re working with local partners to carry out all necessary environmental remediation and ensure our future plans have appropriately considered the local context and adequately protect the community from future environmental degradation. This environmental work is the reason that we’ve started the planning and permitting process so early – taking the necessary time to ensure plans are advanced responsibly, in compliance with all federal, state and local regulations. The approximately 124-acre property is located on Wellington Road in Gainesville, Virginia, and has a history of industrial use that predates Microsoft’s ownership and resulted in soil and groundwater contamination. Cleanup of this pre-existing contamination continues under a longstanding U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) consent order, which outlines the cleanup requirements and mandates ongoing reporting to the EPA. Under government oversight, the prior industrial operator remains responsible for maintaining the site’s groundwater treatment and monitoring systems and addressing the contamination. Microsoft is funding and providing technical support to relocate and modernize the treatment infrastructure so cleanup can continue as property plans advance. Microsoft and the previous industrial operator are coordinating with the EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Prince William County, and other agencies to ensure that our plans comply with all existing regulations and any necessary environmental reviews and approvals are completed before any work moves forward. Additional information about the property’s cleanup history can be found here: EPA RCRA ID: VAD023741705 | US EPA As plans are developed, Microsoft’s approach will be to avoid and minimize impacts on wetlands, waterways, and other natural resources. If impacts cannot be avoided, appropriate permits would be sought, and mitigation measures such as funding for stream and wetland restoration would be incorporated into the project. As construction moves forward, environmental controls will address stormwater, erosion, soil, dust, and waste. Additionally, materials will be evaluated and managed in accordance with applicable requirements. We will continue to share updates with the local community as plans advance and key milestones are reached.

sources.name: Microsoft Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project
sources.excerpt: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project On Thursday, June 18, Microsoft marked an important milestone in La Porte, Indiana, with a groundbreaking event for its new datacenter project, alongside local leaders and community partners. In addition to the datacenter groundbreaking, Microsoft celebrated the signing of a partnership with Ivy Tech Community College to launch its first Microsoft Datacenter Academy in Indiana. The event brought together elected officials, community stakeholders, and partners to highlight progress on site development and reinforce Microsoft’s commitment to investing in the region through jobs, infrastructure, and long-term community engagement. Brad Smith, Microsoft Vice Chair and President, delivered remarks as part of Microsoft’s Community-First Infrastructure initiative, joining the La Porte mayor and local leaders. “AI infrastructure is driving demand for skilled trades nationwide,” said Smith. “We’re committed to helping fill these jobs with people in the communities where we operate. Our Datacenter Academy agreement with Ivy Tech Community College will do just that by equipping people in Indiana with the skills to pursue the jobs we will create here.” Beyond the thousands of construction jobs, the first phase of the new datacenter is expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs. It will grow local tax revenues to support schools and the broader community for generations. The campus will be designed with the latest energy efficient and closed-loop liquid cooling technologies to conserve natural resources. And Microsoft will enhance the surrounding ecosystem to strengthen flood protection and natural habitat.

sources.name: Microsoft Responsible development in Prince William County
sources.excerpt: Responsible development in Prince William County An update on our environmental work at the proposed Wellington datacenter site In 2024, Microsoft purchased land in Prince William County, Virginia for the purpose of datacenter development. While datacenter development has yet to commence, we have started the process of applying for permits. The project remains in the early planning and permitting stage with actual datacenter construction still a long way off. Microsoft is committed to responsible development on this site, respecting the unique and challenging environmental history of this land. We’re working with local partners to carry out all necessary environmental remediation and ensure our future plans have appropriately considered the local context and adequately protect the community from future environmental degradation. This environmental work is the reason that we’ve started the planning and permitting process so early – taking the necessary time to ensure plans are advanced responsibly, in compliance with all federal, state and local regulations. The approximately 124-acre property is located on Wellington Road in Gainesville, Virginia, and has a history of industrial use that predates Microsoft’s ownership and resulted in soil and groundwater contamination. Cleanup of this pre-existing contamination continues under a longstanding U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) consent order, which outlines the cleanup requirements and mandates ongoing reporting to the EPA. Under government oversight, the prior industrial operator remains responsible for maintaining the site’s groundwater treatment and monitoring systems and addressing the contamination. Microsoft is funding and providing technical support to relocate and modernize the treatment infrastructure so cleanup can continue as property plans advance. Microsoft and the previous industrial operator are coordinating with the EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Prince William County, and other agencies to ensure that our plans comply with all existing regulations and any necessary environmental reviews and approvals are completed before any work moves forward. Additional information about the property’s cleanup history can be found here: EPA RCRA ID: VAD023741705 | US EPA As plans are developed, Microsoft’s approach will be to avoid and minimize impacts on wetlands, waterways, and other natural resources. If impacts cannot be avoided, appropriate permits would be sought, and mitigation measures such as funding for stream and wetland restoration would be incorporated into the project. As construction moves forward, environmental controls will address stormwater, erosion, soil, dust, and waste. Additionally, materials will be evaluated and managed in accordance with applicable requirements. We will continue to share updates with the local community as plans advance and key milestones are reached.

Energy The Abilene AI data center connects directly to the ERCOT grid, allowing us to draw from the region's robust and growing supply of renewable energy, including wind, which often goes underutilized in the area. To support grid stability, the Abilene campus uses GE Vernova’s modern natural gas turbines for backup power. The turbines are equipped with Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which transforms nitrogen oxides (NOx) into harmless water vapor and nitrogen through a catalytic converter, producing 90% lower emissions than conventional gas- or diesel-powered reciprocating engines, with little to no methane slip. Water The Abilene AI data center uses a one-time fill, closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system that significantly reduces water consumption. sources.name: Microsoft Alviso datacenter construction update
sources.excerpt: Alviso datacenter construction update Alviso datacenter construction begins in California Microsoft is expanding its datacenter infrastructure with construction at our new Alviso site in California. This update marks the beginning of a multi-phase effort to prepare the land for future datacenter development, supporting the growing demand for cloud services and digital transformation. Why datacenters are needed Datacenters provide the physical infrastructure for the technology we depend on at work and in our personal lives. Whenever you open an app on your phone, join a virtual classroom or meeting, snap and save photos, or play a game with your friends online, you are using a datacenter. Local businesses, government, hospitals, and schools rely on datacenters every day to deliver goods and services to you. Construction overview HITT Contracting Inc. is the general contractor for the Alviso datacenter. Construction began in fall 2025 with initial work focused on earthmoving and soil remediation. Site preparation work is expected to be completed by summer 2026. We’re working closely with HITT to keep neighbors informed ahead of any major construction activity. Construction hours Work will take place Monday through Friday, from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Should additional hours be required, HITT will adhere to the local requirements. Staying connected We’re committed to keeping the community informed. Visit our Microsoft in your community page for updates.

sources.name: Microsoft Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project
sources.excerpt: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project On Thursday, June 18, Microsoft marked an important milestone in La Porte, Indiana, with a groundbreaking event for its new datacenter project, alongside local leaders and community partners. In addition to the datacenter groundbreaking, Microsoft celebrated the signing of a partnership with Ivy Tech Community College to launch its first Microsoft Datacenter Academy in Indiana. The event brought together elected officials, community stakeholders, and partners to highlight progress on site development and reinforce Microsoft’s commitment to investing in the region through jobs, infrastructure, and long-term community engagement. Brad Smith, Microsoft Vice Chair and President, delivered remarks as part of Microsoft’s Community-First Infrastructure initiative, joining the La Porte mayor and local leaders. “AI infrastructure is driving demand for skilled trades nationwide,” said Smith. “We’re committed to helping fill these jobs with people in the communities where we operate. Our Datacenter Academy agreement with Ivy Tech Community College will do just that by equipping people in Indiana with the skills to pursue the jobs we will create here.” Beyond the thousands of construction jobs, the first phase of the new datacenter is expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs. It will grow local tax revenues to support schools and the broader community for generations. The campus will be designed with the latest energy efficient and closed-loop liquid cooling technologies to conserve natural resources. And Microsoft will enhance the surrounding ecosystem to strengthen flood protection and natural habitat.

September 2026: Construction update Work continues to move forward on the first building at the Lyle Creek datacenter site, with key milestones achieved on the building structure and exterior. The building exterior is in its final stages of completion. Framing and drywall work has started and continues to progress throughout the building. Work on underground infrastructure also continues to support the site and upcoming equipment deliveries. Mechanical and electrical work has begun, and additional interior work continues. Work is also beginning on additional building areas to support upcoming phases of construction. We appreciate the community’s patience as construction progresses and will continue to provide updates on significant milestones. May 2026: Construction update Work is advancing across multiple areas of the site, with key milestones reached in foundations and early structural development. Construction activity is moving forward as crews complete early phases and begin vertical construction: Underground work, foundations, and slab installation are complete for several buildings. Steel installation has begun on site, marking the start of above-ground construction. Additional buildings are progressing through foundation and footing stages as site-wide development continues. Telecommunications infrastructure work is underway in multiple areas to support future operations. February 2026: Construction update At the Lyle Creek site, Microsoft’s general contractor, Whiting‑Turner, will begin initial site preparation once weather conditions allow. Early activities will include installing fencing, preparing the site, and limited paving work to support temporary facilities. Foundation work is expected to begin in mid‑March, following completion of site preparation activities. sources.name: Microsoft Responsible development in Prince William County
sources.excerpt: Responsible development in Prince William County An update on our environmental work at the proposed Wellington datacenter site In 2024, Microsoft purchased land in Prince William County, Virginia for the purpose of datacenter development. While datacenter development has yet to commence, we have started the process of applying for permits. The project remains in the early planning and permitting stage with actual datacenter construction still a long way off. Microsoft is committed to responsible development on this site, respecting the unique and challenging environmental history of this land. We’re working with local partners to carry out all necessary environmental remediation and ensure our future plans have appropriately considered the local context and adequately protect the community from future environmental degradation. This environmental work is the reason that we’ve started the planning and permitting process so early – taking the necessary time to ensure plans are advanced responsibly, in compliance with all federal, state and local regulations. The approximately 124-acre property is located on Wellington Road in Gainesville, Virginia, and has a history of industrial use that predates Microsoft’s ownership and resulted in soil and groundwater contamination. Cleanup of this pre-existing contamination continues under a longstanding U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) consent order, which outlines the cleanup requirements and mandates ongoing reporting to the EPA. Under government oversight, the prior industrial operator remains responsible for maintaining the site’s groundwater treatment and monitoring systems and addressing the contamination. Microsoft is funding and providing technical support to relocate and modernize the treatment infrastructure so cleanup can continue as property plans advance. Microsoft and the previous industrial operator are coordinating with the EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Prince William County, and other agencies to ensure that our plans comply with all existing regulations and any necessary environmental reviews and approvals are completed before any work moves forward. Additional information about the property’s cleanup history can be found here: EPA RCRA ID: VAD023741705 | US EPA As plans are developed, Microsoft’s approach will be to avoid and minimize impacts on wetlands, waterways, and other natural resources. If impacts cannot be avoided, appropriate permits would be sought, and mitigation measures such as funding for stream and wetland restoration would be incorporated into the project. As construction moves forward, environmental controls will address stormwater, erosion, soil, dust, and waste. Additionally, materials will be evaluated and managed in accordance with applicable requirements. We will continue to share updates with the local community as plans advance and key milestones are reached.

Community Impact This AI data center will yield an estimated $30 million annually in local economic benefits for the City of Abilene and Taylor County, supporting schools, emergency services, roads, and county programs. Energy The Abilene AI data center connects directly to the ERCOT grid, allowing us to draw from the region's robust and growing supply of renewable energy, including wind, which often goes underutilized in the area. To support grid stability, the Abilene campus uses GE Vernova’s modern natural gas turbines for backup power. The turbines are equipped with Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which transforms nitrogen oxides (NOx) into harmless water vapor and nitrogen through a catalytic converter, producing 90% lower emissions than conventional gas- or diesel-powered reciprocating engines, with little to no methane slip. Water The Abilene AI data center uses a one-time fill, closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system that significantly reduces water consumption. Each building will use roughly 50,000 gallons per year for cooling maintenance, which is under the yearly water use of a single American household—an exceptionally small amount for a facility of this size. sources.name: Microsoft Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project
sources.excerpt: Microsoft breaks ground on La Porte datacenter project On Thursday, June 18, Microsoft marked an important milestone in La Porte, Indiana, with a groundbreaking event for its new datacenter project, alongside local leaders and community partners. In addition to the datacenter groundbreaking, Microsoft celebrated the signing of a partnership with Ivy Tech Community College to launch its first Microsoft Datacenter Academy in Indiana. The event brought together elected officials, community stakeholders, and partners to highlight progress on site development and reinforce Microsoft’s commitment to investing in the region through jobs, infrastructure, and long-term community engagement. Brad Smith, Microsoft Vice Chair and President, delivered remarks as part of Microsoft’s Community-First Infrastructure initiative, joining the La Porte mayor and local leaders. “AI infrastructure is driving demand for skilled trades nationwide,” said Smith. “We’re committed to helping fill these jobs with people in the communities where we operate. Our Datacenter Academy agreement with Ivy Tech Community College will do just that by equipping people in Indiana with the skills to pursue the jobs we will create here.” Beyond the thousands of construction jobs, the first phase of the new datacenter is expected to create more than 600 permanent Microsoft jobs. It will grow local tax revenues to support schools and the broader community for generations. The campus will be designed with the latest energy efficient and closed-loop liquid cooling technologies to conserve natural resources. And Microsoft will enhance the surrounding ecosystem to strengthen flood protection and natural habitat.

sources.name: Microsoft Responsible development in Prince William County
sources.excerpt: Responsible development in Prince William County An update on our environmental work at the proposed Wellington datacenter site In 2024, Microsoft purchased land in Prince William County, Virginia for the purpose of datacenter development. While datacenter development has yet to commence, we have started the process of applying for permits. The project remains in the early planning and permitting stage with actual datacenter construction still a long way off. Microsoft is committed to responsible development on this site, respecting the unique and challenging environmental history of this land. We’re working with local partners to carry out all necessary environmental remediation and ensure our future plans have appropriately considered the local context and adequately protect the community from future environmental degradation. This environmental work is the reason that we’ve started the planning and permitting process so early – taking the necessary time to ensure plans are advanced responsibly, in compliance with all federal, state and local regulations. The approximately 124-acre property is located on Wellington Road in Gainesville, Virginia, and has a history of industrial use that predates Microsoft’s ownership and resulted in soil and groundwater contamination. Cleanup of this pre-existing contamination continues under a longstanding U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) consent order, which outlines the cleanup requirements and mandates ongoing reporting to the EPA. Under government oversight, the prior industrial operator remains responsible for maintaining the site’s groundwater treatment and monitoring systems and addressing the contamination. Microsoft is funding and providing technical support to relocate and modernize the treatment infrastructure so cleanup can continue as property plans advance. Microsoft and the previous industrial operator are coordinating with the EPA, the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Prince William County, and other agencies to ensure that our plans comply with all existing regulations and any necessary environmental reviews and approvals are completed before any work moves forward. Additional information about the property’s cleanup history can be found here: EPA RCRA ID: VAD023741705 | US EPA As plans are developed, Microsoft’s approach will be to avoid and minimize impacts on wetlands, waterways, and other natural resources. If impacts cannot be avoided, appropriate permits would be sought, and mitigation measures such as funding for stream and wetland restoration would be incorporated into the project. As construction moves forward, environmental controls will address stormwater, erosion, soil, dust, and waste. Additionally, materials will be evaluated and managed in accordance with applicable requirements. We will continue to share updates with the local community as plans advance and key milestones are reached.

Community Impact This AI data center will yield an estimated $30 million annually in local economic benefits for the City of Abilene and Taylor County, supporting schools, emergency services, roads, and county programs. Energy The Abilene AI data center connects directly to the ERCOT grid, allowing us to draw from the region's robust and growing supply of renewable energy, including wind, which often goes underutilized in the area. To support grid stability, the Abilene campus uses GE Vernova’s modern natural gas turbines for backup power. The turbines are equipped with Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which transforms nitrogen oxides (NOx) into harmless water vapor and nitrogen through a catalytic converter, producing 90% lower emissions than conventional gas- or diesel-powered reciprocating engines, with little to no methane slip. Water The Abilene AI data center uses a one-time fill, closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system that significantly reduces water consumption. Bourgeois, secretary of Louisiana Economic Development. “From preparing Louisianans for high-paying careers to putting our local companies in the pipeline for contracts, we are focused on making sure investments of this scale create opportunity that reaches well beyond the project site. The real measure of a project like this is how broadly its benefits are felt, and we are working to ensure they reach workers, businesses, and communities across Louisiana.” When fully built out, the three planned campuses are expected to create up to 750 full-time jobs at Amazon data centers and support 2,500 additional positions in the broader community. These roles include electricians, HVAC technicians, project engineers, network specialists, operations managers, security specialists, and other skilled positions offering competitive pay and comprehensive benefits. sources.excerpt: newly rebuilt deck for a resident during the United Way of Richmond County's annual Days of Caring. Amazon is building a new data center campus in Richmond County, North Carolina, but the team didn't wait for operations to begin to start getting involved. From September 16–18, 45 employees fanned out across the county for the United Way of Richmond County's annual Days of Caring, volunteering on three projects and logging nearly 170 hours combined. Feeding kids on the weekends The team spent the morning with Backpack Pals, assembling more than 450 weekend meal kits for children across Richmond County schools. The kits make sure students have something to eat when the cafeteria isn't an option. Many of our employees are parents, so this project was personal. Making Ms. Vickie's home accessible again Part of the team joined Habitat for Humanity of the NC Sandhills for a multiday volunteer effort to demolish and rebuild three decks for Ms. Vickie, a local resident who could no longer safely get in and out of her home. Our team was proud to be part of the crew that made her home accessible again. Getting the food pantry ready The rest of the team deep-cleaned and restocked Our Daily Bread Food Ministry's food pantry from floor to ceiling—organizing shelves, rotating inventory, and preparing it to serve the families who depend on it most.
